difficulty.reason: Setting up Stripe Connect OAuth requires navigating the Stripe Dashboard, configuring branding, redirect URIs, and handling Stripe's specific OAuth token exchange flows, though the developer setup itself is relatively fast once authenticated.

timeEstimate.approvalWait: Instant to minimal (test mode is immediate; live mode verification depends on business validation)
timeEstimate.notes: Test mode OAuth applications can be used immediately. Live mode activation requires business verification with Stripe, which can take anywhere from a few hours to a few days.

requirements: Configured redirect URIs in the Stripe Dashboard
HTTPS-enabled redirect endpoints (required for production/live mode)

steps.title: Create a Stripe Account
steps.description: Sign up for a Stripe account and access the Stripe Dashboard.

steps.title: Configure Stripe Connect Settings
steps.description: Navigate to the Connect settings page in your Stripe Dashboard to enable Connect and configure your platform settings.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URIs and Branding
steps.description: Set up your application's redirect URIs (Callback URLs), business name, icon, and branding that users will see during the OAuth consent flow.

steps.title: Obtain Client ID and API Keys
steps.description: Retrieve your unique `client_id` (e.g., `ca_...`) for initiating OAuth authorization requests and your Secret Key for token exchange.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth Flow
steps.description: Redirect users to Stripe's authorize endpoint (`https://connect.stripe.com/oauth/authorize`) with your `client_id`, `response_type=code`, and optional scope, then exchange the returned authorization code via a POST request to `https://connect.stripe.com/oauth/token`.

blockers.problem: Using HTTP instead of HTTPS for redirect URIs in production.
blockers.solution: Stripe enforces HTTPS for all live mode redirect URIs. Ensure your callback endpoints possess valid SSL certificates.

blockers.problem: Confusing standard Stripe API keys with Stripe Connect OAuth Client IDs.
blockers.solution: Ensure you use the Connect `client_id` (starting with `ca_`) for generating the authorization URL, rather than your standard API secret key.

agentCanDo: Generate OAuth authorization URLs with correct query parameters
Handle the authorization code callback parsing
Execute the backend POST request to exchange authorization codes for access tokens
Refresh tokens and manage token storage state
developerMustDo: Log into the Stripe Dashboard with 2FA
Set up and verify business details for Stripe account activation
Configure allowed redirect URIs and platform branding in the Stripe Dashboard
Provision secure backend infrastructure to store client secrets

managedOption.managedSufficientWhen: Building a quick prototype, internal AI agent tool, or generic integration where users connect their own Stripe accounts via a unified auth provider (like Composio or LangChain integrations) without custom branding.
managedOption.customRequiredWhen: Building a dedicated SaaS product or multi-tenant agent platform that requires white-labeled Stripe Connect onboarding, custom platform branding, and direct control over Connected Accounts.

claims.claim: Stripe Connect uses standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant flow with authorize and token endpoints.
Test mode OAuth apps can be configured and tested instantly without waiting for business verification.

openQuestions: Are there any specific third-party security assessments (like CASA) mandated by Stripe for public Connect platforms, or is standard Stripe platform review sufficient?
